newsitem.title: CHINA: China rice prices seen stable, corn low.
newsitem.headline: China rice prices seen stable, corn low.

text.p: China forecast the domestic rice price would be stable in the near future while corn prices are seen depressed because of low international prices, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.
Rice on the open market was now stable at a price slightly lower than the state purchase price, but would rise if central and local governments expanded their reserves, the newspaper said.
Corn prices were expected to stay well below state purchase levels due to low international prices, it quoted the State Grains and Edible Oil Information Center as saying.
Corn in production areas was selling for about 1,100 yuan ($132) a tonne while the state price was 1,250 yuan per tonne, it said.
Wheat prices would be stable if imports this year were close to last year's level, but could rise to slightly above the state purchase price, it said.
Prices of soybeans could fall in the first half of the year and pick up later amid a continuing tight market, it said, but gave no further details.
